messages:
sam: heads-up: canary pool v2.18 shows a sudden OOM spike after last merge (PR #5423) — 6 failures in 2h :frowning:
laura: saw the alerts, all on canary nodes (g5.xlarge), seqlen skew >8k on a subset of requests
tariq: initial hunch: adaptive-evict math from #5423 changed the windowing and might interact with prefetch
sam: repro on my devbox with KV_EVICT_WINDOW=0.65 -> OOM at ~7k tokens (was stable to ~12k before)
miguel: CI flagged this too — runtime-bench-longctx memory reg in 2026-03-15T08:12 run
ops-bot: CI perf run 2026-03-15T08:12 flagged a 3% mem regression on runtime-bench-longctx
jessica: paste of recent libc logs from one failed shard:
[pid 1234] mmap(0x0, 8388608, PROT_READ|PROT_WRITE, MAP_PRIVATE|MAP_ANONYMOUS, -1, 0) = -1 ENOMEM
sam: attaching pprof summary from failing run:
```text
(pprof) top
700MB  35%  runtime.kv_slab.alloc
400MB  20%  runtime.kv_map.resize
250MB  12%  runtime.kv_refcount_table
```
laura: also seeing fragmentation in /proc/<pid>/smaps: lots of anon huge pages with small used/resident chunks
tariq: timeline check: #5401 (kernel-router fallback changes) merged -> #5423 (evict/prefetch) merged -> canary rollout -> OOMs start
sam: suggestion: bisect by reverting #5423 on canary and rerunning seqlen-heavy smoke
miguel: I reverted #5423 on canary-2 earlier, OOMs dropped to zero in ~1 hour after revert
sam: confirm numbers: after revert memory per-inference dropped ~30% on 10k seqlen runs
tariq: note #5423 added batch-boundary prefetch + adjusted evict threshold. Could be duplicate KV refs when prefetch + kernel-switch overlap
jessica: small repro command I used:
```bash
export REDWOOD_KV_PREFETCH=1
./runtime_bench --model llama-13b --seq 11000 --concurrency 2 --runs 20
```
miguel: heap profile from failing run shows many retained objects in slab allocator buckets:
```text
(pprof) list kv_slab
Total: 1.2GB
400MB  runtime.kv_slab.allocate_item
...
```
laura: metric kv.cache.entries_count spikes then drops quickly — mass evictions then re-inserts pattern
sam: hypothesis: prefetch triggers + autobatch boundary increase hold KV entries longer; kernel-router fallback can cause same tensors to be referenced twice (duplicated lifetime) -> fragmentation and slow coalescing
tariq: also possible refcount accounting bug introduced when prefetch path touches KV concurrently with kernel migration path
jessica: I'll add a test-only refcount assert in KV lookup code and run race-mode reproducer (will push a branch: debug/kv-ref-assert)
miguel: short-term action: hold rollout and pin dedicated/canary to previous image; I filed INC-2026-114 and paused canary rollout
ops-bot: Rollout paused for canary group redwood-canary-2 by miguel at 08:50
sam: we should also add a post-merge long-seq memory guard in CI to catch regressions like this
laura: another angle: autobatch change prefers larger batches -> increases aggregate KV live set and delays eviction windows; mixing short+long seqs amplifies fragmentation
tariq: agreed. add unit test that simulates variance: 90% short, 10% long and assert mem delta stays within budget
jessica: coordinating with eng-ml to run an A/B: kernel-router v1 (old fallback) vs v2 + prefetch v2 to confirm interaction matrix
miguel: since revert removed the issue in canary, let's keep rollout paused until we ship a fix and CI test
sam: long term fix: (1) patch refcount pathology in KV, (2) revise prefetch window heuristics to cap overlap with kernel-switch, (3) add CI long-seq mem regression test
laura: summary for incident notes: root cause = interaction between prefetch/batch-window changes in PR #5423 and kernel-router fallback changes in #5401 causing duplicated KV lifetimes -> fragmentation -> OOM on long sequences. Verified by revert on canary.
tariq: next steps: jessica PR with assert (debug), sam PR for CI guard, miguel keep rollout paused, laura follow up on autobatch tuning and coalescing heuristics
sam: thanks all :thumbsup:
